The Saviynt Identity Cloud APIs are versioned APIs. Any updates to a version are considered non-breaking to ensure the integration do not break. Breaking changes such as an addition of a new required field will be released as a new version of the API.

Syntax used in the API URLs:

{{url}}/ECM/{{path}}/apiName

Set the variables to match your Saviynt Identity Cloud environment

  • {{url}}: Enter the Saviynt Identity Cloud application URL in the following format: https://SUBDOMAIN.saviyntcloud.com
    For example: https://myorg.saviyntcloud.com

  • {{path}}: Enter api/v5.

  • {path2}}: Enter api/certifications/v2/items.

Note:

  • If Content-Type in the response header needs to be overriden, add an entry in configuration table in database with name as 'api.v5.response.contenttype' and configdata as any valid content-type (application/json, application/xml etc.)

  • The Web Application Firewall (WAF) limit for Saviynt Identity Cloud is 5000/IP/5minutes. This limit ensures that the network traffic communicating with Saviynt Identity Cloud is legitimate, and enhances security.

request.description:
The Bearer Authentication scheme is dedicated to token authentication and is described by RFC6750. Even if this scheme comes from an OAuth2 specification, you can still use it to exchange tokens between a client and a server.

The API requires the HTTP authentication scheme Bearer for authentication. All requests must have a valid Token specified in the HTTP Authorization header with the Bearer scheme.

Mandatory Parameters

  • username: Specify the user name to log in to Saviynt Identity Cloud.

  • password: Specify the password to log in to Saviynt Identity Cloud.

A POST request, in which the username and password are passed in JSON text in the body, will return a Token in the response, which can be passed in a header variable for subsequent requests.

Note: You can now use the Basic Auth (basic authentication) method to authenticate the Login API (/api/login). To do so, select Basic Auth from the Type drop-down list on the Authorization tab and enter your login credentials in the Username and Password fields.

Refresh Token Properties

You can manage the following refresh token properties from the externalconfig.properties file on the Configuration Files page (Admin > Settings > Configuration Files).

Property Description
grails.plugin.springsecurity.rest.token.storage.jwt.expiration Specify the time after which the access token expires.
grails.plugin.springsecurity.rest.refreshtoken.storage.jwt.expiration Specify the time after which the refresh token expires. The refresh token expires after the specified interval and can no longer be used to get a new access token.
grails.plugin.springsecurity.rest.refreshtoken.new Specify true to generate a new token after the refresh token expires.

For more information about updating the externalconfig.properties file, see Managing Configuration Files in the Enterprise Identity Cloud Administration Guide.

request.description:
The Saviynt Identity Cloud supports OAuth2.0, the industry-standard authorization protocol. It focuses on client developer simplicity while providing specific authorization flows for web applications. For more information, see OAuth 2.0 documentation.

Note: Refresh tokens are long-lived tokens. However, they can be invalidated at any time, and your application must be designed to handle a refresh token invalidation gracefully. This can be done by obtaining a new access or refresh token using your login credentials, either interactively with user input or programmatically without explicit user action.

item.name: Exchange the Authorization Code for Subject Token

request.description:
After you have acquired an authorization code, you can exchange it for a subject token (access or ID tokens).

Note: You must configure your external Identity Provider (IdP), integrate your OIDC application with Saviynt Identity Cloud, and generate the OpenID authorization code. For more information, see Configuring OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange Authentication in the Enterprise Identity Cloud Administration Guide.

Mandatory URL Parameter

domainURL: Specify the OpenID Connect IdP's authorization endpoint URL.

Example: https://companyname.okta.com/oauth2/v1/token

Mandatory Parameters

  • grant_type: Specify authorization_code as the grant type for the authorization code flow.

  • redirect_uri: Specify the URI that was used to obtain the authorization code.

  • code: Specify the authorization code you obtained.

  • client_id: Specify the client ID that was generated for your registered application in the IdP.

  • client_secret: Specify the client secret that was generated for your registered application in the IdP.

request.description:
After acquiring the access or ID token described in Exchange the Authorization Code for Subject Token, you can exchange them with the Saviynt Identity Cloud tokens to authenticate and authorize users for Saviynt APIs.

Note: You must configure your external Identity Provider (IdP), integrate your OIDC application with Saviynt Identity Cloud, and generate the OpenID authorization code. For more information, see Configuring OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange Authentication in the Enterprise Identity Cloud Administration Guide.

Mandatory Parameters

  • grant_type: Specify urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange as the grant type to request the access token.

  • subject_token: Specify the access or ID token from the Authorization Code flow you obtained in Exchange the Authorization Code for Subject Token.

  • subject_token_type: The type of subject token issued by the IdP in Exchange the Authorization Code for Subject Token. Specify one of the following token types:

    • urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token: Indicates that the token is an OAuth 2.0 access token.

    • urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token: Indicates that the token is an ID token.
      For example, if you specify an access token for the subject_token parameter, enter urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token as the subject token type.

  • scope: Specify the Oauth_token_exchange connector you created while integrating your OIDC application with Saviynt Identity Cloud.

Use this API to create and update users using bulk upload.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory Parameter

file - Provide the CSV file and select the key field type as File.

Optional Parameters

  • delimiter - tab, pipe, comma. Default value is comma.

  • zeroDayProvisioning - YES/NO. Default value is NO.

  • generateSystemUsername - YES/NO. Default value is NO.

  • generateEmail - YES/NO. Default value is NO.

  • checkrules - YES/NO. Default value is NO.

  • checkruleforcustomjar- YES/NO. Default value is NO. This option helps in checking whether a pre-validation is required while uploading users, on the basis of the logic defined in the Saviynt validation framework extension (JAR) file.

  • expirepasswordfornewuser- YES/NO. Default value is NO.

  • userReconcillationField - Text field.

  • userpreprocessorconfigjson - Text field.ok

Use this API to return a list of all users in Saviynt Identity Cloud.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Optional Parameters

  • username - Specify the username for which you want to get the user attribute details.

  • responsefields - User attributes which you want to see in the response(for encrypted values, mention ecp<1-5>, and for hashed values, mention hcp<1-5>).

  • max: Specify the maximum number of results that can be returned in the response. The maximum number that you can specify is 500.

  • offset: Specify the the starting point (index) from which to start retrieval. The minimum value that you can specify is 1 .

  • sort: Specify the order in which results are returned in the response. If no order is specified then default value is username.

  • order: The order in which the sorting is performed. For example asc (default) or desc order.

  • manager: Specify the username of the manager.

  • secondarymanager: Specify the userkey or username of the user's secondary manager.

  • showsecurityanswers - "0"/"1" to display encrypted security answers for the user

  • filtercriteria - User fields based on which you want to get the user attribute details(including userkey),

  • searchCriteria - search for a user based on the string passed (eg - “*ab*” or “*ab” or “ab*”) in their firstname, lastname, displayname and username only, example - "ab*" - This will return all users with firstname or lastname or username starting with "ab"

  • advsearchcriteria : Search for a user based on the string passed (eg - “*ab*” or “*ab” or “ab*”), example - {"username":"a*", "firstname":"*b"} - This will return all users with username starting with "a" AND firstname ending with "b". Exact match search is applicable for types boolean, users, customer. Date can be entered in format - yyyy-MM-dd.

  • userQuery: Specify the user query. For example: “userQuery”:”user.customproperty1='abc' or user.displayname like '%display%'”

Note - By default, if no responsefields param is passed, required attrs that will always return are username, email, statuskey, firstname, lastname, employeeid along with other attributes with nonblank values only.

UserName

This method returns a List of "Accounts" in SSM.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Optional params:
username,
endpoint,
max,
offset,
accountQuery,
advsearchcriteria - accountKey,description,comments,accounttype,status,customproperty1-customproperty56,accountID,displayName,name,creator (username),updateuser (username),validfromDate validthrough,createdon,lastlogondate,lastpasswordchange,updatedate,orphan (true/false),
accountowner - with fields 1. type - user/ usergroup (mandatory), 2. value - username/ usergroup name (mandatory), 3. rank - 1 to 5 (optional)

Sample - "advsearchcriteria":{ "status":"ACTIVE","name":"john*","createdon":"2016-12-13","customproperty12":"*Ro*","orphan":"true","accountowner": [
{
"type": "user",
"value": "janedoe",
"rank": "1"
}
]},

Date can be searched with 'yyyy-MM-dd', dates and boolean are exact match.

Note: Any OR conditions must be used within parenthesis. For example:

{
"accountQuery":"(acc.status='1' or acc.comments like '%a%')",
"username":"admin"
}

entquery - query to support parent entitlement_values parameters. Sample - "pev.status = 1",

max,

offset

This method creates a new "entitlementvalue" for an "endpoint" in SSM. All the input parameters it requires are attributes with which the new account record would get created.

Ensure: The Authorization header variable must be set to Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

endpoint, entitlementtype, entitlement_value

Optional params:

attributes for Entitlement_values,

entitlementowner<N> - N is the rank, entitlementowner modifies entitlementowner with rank 1, entitlementowner3 - modifies entitlementowner with rank 3,

entitlementID,newentitlement_value - used to update the entitlement if multiple entitlements with same entitlement_value are present under the same entitlementtype and endpoint

entitlementcasecheck(can be true or false, default : false) - If true, entitlement value search will be case sensitive during create or update.

entitlement_valuekey

updatedentitlement_value - new value for entitlement_value

entitlementmap -

  1. entitlementvalue
  2. entitlementtype
  3. endpoint
  4. requestfilter
  5. excludeentitlement
  6. adddependenttask
  7. removedependententtask
  8. updateType(ADD/REMOVE, default : ADD)

request.description:
Use this API to create an endpoint in EIC.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Mandatory Parameters

  • endpointname: Specify a name for the endpoint. Provide a logical name that will help you easily identify it.

  • displayName: Enter a user-friendly display name for the endpoint that will be displayed in the user interface. Display Name can be different from Endpoint Name.

  • securitysystem: Specify the Security system for which you want to create an endpoint.

Optional Parameters

  • description: Specify a description for the endpoint.

  • ownerType: Specify the owner type for the endpoint. An endpoint can be owned by a User or Usergroup.

  • owner: Specify the owner of the endpoint. If the ownerType is User, then specify the username of the owner, and If it is is Usergroup then specify the name of the user group.

  • resourceOwnerType: Specify the resource owner type for the endpoint. An endpoint can be owned by a User or Usergroup.

  • resourceOwner: Specify the resource owner of the endpoint. If the resourceOwnerType is User, then specify the username of the owner and If it is Usergroup, specify the name of the user group.

  • accessquery: Specify the query to filter the access and display of the endpoint to specific users. If you do not define a query, the endpoint is displayed for all users.

  • enableCopyAccess: Specify true to display the Copy Access from User option in the Request pages.

  • createEntTaskforRemoveAccEnd: If this is set to true, remove Access tasks will be created for entitlements (account entitlements and their dependent entitlements) when a user requests for removing an account.

  • disableNewAccountRequestIfAccountExists: Specify true to disable users from requesting additional accounts on applications where they already have active accounts.

  • disableRemoveAccount: Specify true to disable users from removing their existing application accounts.

  • disableModifyAccount: Specify true to disable users from modifying their application accounts.

  • blockInflightRequest: Specify true to prevent users from raising duplicate requests for the same applications.

  • accountNameRule: Specify rule to generate an account name for this endpoint while creating a new account.

  • userAccountCorrelationRule: Specify rule to map users in EIC with the accounts during account import.

  • connectionconfig: Use this configuration for processing the add access tasks and remove access tasks for AD and LDAP Connectors.

  • customproperty1 to customproperty45: Custom properties 1 to 45.

  • customproperty1Label to customproperty45Label: Specify the labels for the custom properties of accounts associated with this endpoint.

  • parentAccountPattern: Specify the parent and child relationship for the Active Directory endpoint. The specified value is used to filter the parent and child objects in the Request Access tile.

  • serviceAccountAccessQuery: Specify the query to filter the access and display of the endpoint for specific users while managing service accounts

  • allowRemoveAllRoleOnRequest: Specify true to displays the Remove All Roles option in the Request page that can be used to remove all the roles.

  • changePasswordAccessQuery: Specify query to restrict the access for changing the account password of the endpoint.

  • accountNameValidatorRegex: Specify the regular expression which will be used to validate the account name either generated by the rule or provided manually.

  • statusConfig: Specify to enable the State and Status options (Enable, Disable, Lock, Unlock) that would be available to request for a user and service accounts.

  • pluginConfigs: The Plugin Configuration drives the functionality of the Saviynt SmartAssist (Browserplugin).

  • endpointConfig: Specify to copy data in Step 3 of the service account request will be enabled.

  • primaryAccountType: If a user has multiple account types for an endpoint (for example, User, Service, or Privileged accounts), specify the account type for which you want to restrict the assignment of entitlements.

  "endpointname": "myorgendpoint",

  "ownerType": "User",

  "enableCopyAccess": "true",

request.description:
Use this API to update an endpoint in EIC.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Note: From Release v23.9, a new parameter requestableRoleType is introduced to update the requestable options of a Role for a particular endpoint.

Mandatory Parameters

  • endpointname: Specify a name for the endpoint. Provide a logical name that will help you easily identify it.

Optional Parameters

  • displayName: Enter a user-friendly display name for the endpoint that will be displayed in the user interface. Display Name can be different from Endpoint Name.

  • securitysystem: Specify the Security system for which you want to create an endpoint.

  • description: Specify a description for the endpoint.

  • ownerType: Specify the owner type for the endpoint. An endpoint can be owned by a User or Usergroup.

  • owner: Specify the owner of the endpoint. If the ownerType is User, then specify the username of the owner, and If it is is Usergroup then specify the name of the user group.

  • resourceOwnerType: Specify the resource owner type for the endpoint. An endpoint can be owned by a User or Usergroup.

  • resourceOwner: Specify the resource owner of the endpoint. If the resourceOwnerType is User, then specify the username of the owner and If it is Usergroup, specify the name of the user group.

  • accessquery: Specify the query to filter the access and display of the endpoint to specific users. If you do not define a query, the endpoint is displayed for all users.

  • enableCopyAccess: Specify true to display the Copy Access from User option in the Request pages.

  • createEntTaskforRemoveAccEnd: If this is set to true, remove Access tasks will be created for entitlements (account entitlements and their dependent entitlements) when a user requests for removing an account.

  • disableNewAccountRequestIfAccountExists: Specify true to disable users from requesting additional accounts on applications where they already have active accounts.

  • disableRemoveAccount: Specify true to disable users from removing their existing application accounts.

  • disableModifyAccount: Specify true to disable users from modifying their application accounts.

  • blockInflightRequest: Specify true to prevent users from raising duplicate requests for the same applications.

  • accountNameRule: Specify rule to generate an account name for this endpoint while creating a new account.

  • userAccountCorrelationRule: Specify rule to map users in EIC with the accounts during account import.

  • connectionconfig: Use this configuration for processing the add access tasks and remove access tasks for AD and LDAP Connectors.

  • customproperty1 to customproperty45: Custom properties 1 to 45.

  • customproperty1Label to customproperty45Label: Specify the labels for the custom properties of accounts associated with this endpoint.

  • allowRemoveAllRoleOnRequest: Specify true to displays the Remove All Roles option in the Request page that can be used to remove all the roles.

  • changePasswordAccessQuery: Specify query to restrict the access for changing the account password of the endpoint.

  • accountNameValidatorRegex: Specify the regular expression which will be used to validate the account name either generated by the rule or provided manually.

  • statusConfig: Specify to enable the State and Status options (Enable, Disable, Lock, Unlock) that would be available to request for a user and service accounts.

  • pluginConfigs: The Plugin Configuration drives the functionality of the Saviynt SmartAssist (Browserplugin).

  • endpointConfig: Specify to copy data in Step 3 of the service account request will be enabled.

  • requestOption - Supports valid case-senstive string values such as “None”, “DropDownSingle”, “Table”, and “TableOnlyAdd”

  • required - Supports valid boolean values are true and falserequestedQuery/selectedQuery Supports string values in double quotes

  • showOn - Supports valid case-sensitive string values such as "All", "ShowOnApplicationRequest", and "ShowOnServiceAccountRequest". specify the value to display the roles on Application Requests, Service Account Requests, or both.

  • emailTemplate: Specify an email template and associate it with a task to use it for sending emails based on the status of the task. Task types such as New Account, Add Access, Remove Account, New Account, and New Account with a password must be configured before they are associated with email templates.

  • primaryAccountType: If a user has multiple account types for an endpoint (for example, User, Service, or Privileged accounts), specify the account type for which you want to restrict the assignment of entitlements.

dynamicattributes - other dynamic attribute parameters:

  • attributetype: Specify the attribute type based on which you want to filter and display the dynamic attributes.The various types of attribute types are: Single select from Sql Query, ENUM, Password, Boolean (True,False), String, Check Box, Date, and so on.

  • attributename: Specify the dynamic attribute name to be used for filtering out and calling the respective attribute to be displayed.

  • Attribute Group: Attribute Group provides you an option to group or categorize and display the dynamic attributes in the Access Requests request form.

  • Order Index: Specify the sequence where you want to display the dynamic attributes. You can specify values such as 0,1, 2, 3 and so on. Order index with lower values is displayed first and those with higher values are displayed later.

  • attributelable: Specify the name of the attribute, which you want to display in the Access Requests request form. You can apply the following font styling to the label:

    • ##SavBoldStart##Attribute_Name##SavBoldEnd##

    • ##SavUnderlineStart##Attribute_Name##SavItalicEnd##

    • ##SavUnderlineStart##Attribute_Name##UnderlineEnd##

    • ##SavAnchorStart####SavUrlStart##https://exampleorg.com##SavUrlEnd####SavUrlTextStart##URL_Text##SavUrlTextEnd####SavAnchorEnd##

  • reconApplication: Specify true to importing data from respective endpoint associated to security system.

  • provisioningTries: Specify the number of times that you want a pending task to be tried for provisioning.

  • instantprovision: Specify true to prevent users from raising duplicate requests for the same applications.

  • provisioningcomments: Specify relevant comments for performing provisioning.

request.description:
Use this API to fetch all organizations (primary and secondary) associated with a user.

Note:

  • You must enable the Enable Multiple Organizations for a User option from the Global Configurations page in the EIC user interface to fetch organizations associated a user.

  • Starting with Release v24.7, this API now retrieves the start date and end date for new or existing users that belong to the secondary organization.EndFragment

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory Parameters:

username: Specify the name of the user whose associated organization details you want to fetch.

Optional Parameters:

  • verbose : Specify true to get additional information of the user like organizationname, displayname, description, or status.

  • fetchonlycount : Specify to get the total count information in response. Example, true or false.

  • orgmemebership : Specify if you want only details from a particular type of organization. Example, primary or secondary).

Use this API to delete an organization in EIC.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

StartFragment

Mandatory Parameters:

  • organizationname

  • username

request.description:
Use this API to to create a connection in Saviynt Identity Cloud.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory Parameters

  • connectionname: Specify the name to identify the connection.

  • connectiontype: Specify a connection type. For example, if your target application is Active Directory, specify the connection type as AD.

Optional Parameters:

The following are the most of the common parameters specified for establishing a connection with a target system.

  • description: Specify the description for the connection.

  • defaultsavroles: Specify the SAV role or combination of Sav roles. This SAV roles must have permissions that the users need for managing this connection along with its associated security systems, endpoints, accounts, and entitlements.

  • emailTemplate: Specify the email template applicable for notifications.

  • sslCertificate: Specify the SSL certificates to use for securing the connection between EIC and the target application to encrypt the data shared between them.

  • vaultConfiguration: Specify the path of the vault to obtain the secret data. Suffix the name of the connector to this path to make it unique for the connector.

  • saveinvault: Specify true to save the encrypted attribute in the vault configured with the connector.

Note that your connection might use some or all of these parameters. Some connectors include additional parameters. For example, If AD is the connection type then there are additional parameters such as, SEARCHFILTER, LDAP_OR_AD, STATUS_THRESHOLD_CONFIG, and so on.

Use this API to return a list of users associated with a specific SAV role in Saviynt Identity Cloud.

This API is used to fetch runtime analytics data from SSM.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params: analyticsid OR analyticsname, attributes - runtime control params. Sample : For this query - select * from users where manager = ${manager} and username = ${username} "attributes":{ "manager":"4", "username":"johndoe" }

Optional params: max, offset, loggedinuser

This API is used to fetch runtime analytics data from ES.

Starting with Release v24.6, the response does not alert users if control execution exceeds 55 seconds. Instead, the control will continue processing normally and deliver results as expected.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

  • analyticsid OR analyticsname((if both are passed then analyticsid will be considered)

  • attributes - runtime control parameters.

Note: Ensure that any runtime control parameter of type date has the following format: "YYYY-MM-DD".

Sample : For this query - SELECT u.username, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.manager AS 'USERCONTEXT',u.statuskey FROM users u WHERE u.statuskey is not null and u.statuskey not in (${statuskey}) and u.MANAGER is not null;
"attributes":{
"statuskey": "0"
}

Optional params:
max,
offset,
requestor

[Updated on 22 October, 2025]

Starting from 24.9 GA

  • Request : Return Latest Analytics History - Returns the most recent analytics history generated at the time of the API request.

Concurrent Analytics Requests:

When two requests are made simultaneously to run the same analytics, each request processes the analytics independently. The API will return the historical data each request generates in its response.

If the history to keep setting is set to 1 or is less than the number of concurrent requests, older history may be deleted during simultaneous execution. In this case, the API will respond with the following message: Due to a concurrent request, the history for this session was deleted. Please call the API again to retrieve the latest history.

Note: To avoid conflicts, it is advisable to invoke API requests sequentially, waiting for the response of each call before making the subsequent request.

  • analyticsHistoryKey
    A new analyticsHistoryKey parameter is now supported in the API request and response, and should be used for pagination when retrieving large analytics history datasets.

    • To ensure data consistency, especially for paginated results, the API will now ALWAYS return an analyticsHistoryKey corresponding to the analytics history. If this analyticsHistoryKey is included in a subsequent API payload, the service will retrieve data from the same history instance instead of re-running the analytics.

    • Pagination-

      • First Call: The initial API call executes the analytics and returns the first page of data, along with a history key.

      • Subsequent Calls: To fetch additional pages from the same dataset, the user must include the previously received historyKey in the request payload, along with the max and offset parameters.

    • Benefit: By providing the historyKey, the API retrieves data from the same history instance, eliminating the need to re-run the analytics. This guarantees data consistency across paginated results and improves performance for large datasets.

When two requests are made simultaneously to run the same analytics, each request processes the analytics independently. Each API call will return the analytics history that corresponds to the most recent history generated at the time of that API call.

request.description:
This API is used to run analytics ES job.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params: jobgroup, jobname, analyticsid OR analyticsname OR analyticsCategories (start and end with ###),

Optional params: analyticssubcategories (start and end with ###)

This API is used for fetching the details of dynamic attributes associated with an analytics control. This can be used for both Elasticsearch and Database analytics.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:
analyticstype(ES/DB)
analyticsname OR id

response.name: Fetch Control Attributes

request.description:
This API performs the action specified under the Default_Action_For_Analytics parameter and retrieves records starting from the offset.

This API can return the response even if the offset parameter is set beyond 1000.

Now, the response of this API displays an additional offset attribute.

Starting with Release v24.1, the behavior of this API has been modified as follows:

  • For newly created analytics controls: You can swiftly execute and retrieve the history of newly created analytics controls.

  • For previously existing analytics controls: To expedite fetching the run history of previously existing analytics controls, you must initially run the control on the Analytics Configuration List page within the user interface. Subsequently, you can use the API to fetch the run history.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

  • controlId - this is the ANALYTICSKEY

  • offset- Specify the value from where the records must be retrieved

Optional params:

max

request.description:
Use this API to update an existing enterprise role created in the Saviynt Identity Cloud.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Mandatory Parameters

  • roletype: Specify ENTERPRISE as the roletype to update the request for an enterprise role.

  • role_name: Specify the name to identify the role.

Optional Parameters

  • requestor: Specify the user for whom you are requesting an enterprise role.

  • owner

    • ownerName: Specify the role owner name.

    • updateType: Specify ADD to assign a role owner to the role or REMOVE to remove the role owner from the role.

  • childRoles
    Note: Available from the Brisbane release.

    • rolename: Specify the child role name.

    • updateType: Specify ADD to add a new child to the parent role and REMOVE to remove a child role.

  • customproperty<1 to 60>: Specify a custom property that can be added for the role.

  • endpointname: Specify the endpoint name associated with this role.

  • entitlements:

    • entitlement_value

    • entitlementType

    • endpoint

    • updateType: ADD/REMOVE

    • privileges: Specify the following values:

      • attributename: Specify the attribute name. The attribute name identifies the privilege name to be used for filtering out and calling the respective privilege to be displayed.

      • attributevalue: Specify the value you want to display for the attribute. The specified value will be selected when the user has not selected any value for this attribute on the request form.

  • rank<1 to 27>

  • defaulttimeframe: Specify the default time (in hours) to request access for a role

  • description: Specify the description of the role.

  • displayname: Specify the display name.

  • glossary: Specify the appropriate glossary.

  • risk: Specify the risk level for the role required for segregation of duties, based on the roles.

  • level: Specify the hierarchy level of this role.

  • soxcritical: Specify the level of roles or policies critically compliant with Sarbanes-Oxley IT regulations.

  • syscritical: Specify the criticality level of roles within the system.

  • privileged: Specify the privilege mapped to the role and its criticality for granting the role access during approval.

  • confidentiality: Specify the level of confidentiality the role has, helping the role owner approve or reject requests based on this parameter.

  • requestable: Specify whether users should request the role.

  • showDynamicAttrs: Displays the dynamic attributes associated with the role.

Note: If the Role Modification Workflow global configuration parameter (Admin > Global Configuration > Roles) is not set, the request will not be created. For more information, see Configuring Roles in the Saviynt Identity Cloud Administration Guide.

Warning Messages

The following warnings can be returned in the message field of the API response:

Error Description
Passed entitlement value(s) {{comma separated entitlement values}} do not exist. The entitlement_value specified does not exist.
Entitlement {entitlement_value} not added to role, so cannot remove it. The entitlement_value specified is not associated with the role.
Entitlement {entitlement_value} already present. The specified entitlement that you want to add already exists.
Endpoint {endpoint_name} not found. The specified endpoint name associated with the role does not exist.
Entitlement Type {entitlementType} not found. The entitlementType specified in the payload does not exist.
Update type {entitlementUpdateType} is not valid. If you specify any value other than ADD or REMOVE for the updatetype.

This API call can be used to fetch the request history of all the requests submitted by an user.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

username - Requestor's username

Optional params:

status - OPEN/DRAFT/INPROCESS/COMPLETED/EXPIRED/DISCONTINUED. For example: as a list ["open","expired"] or a single status like "open",

requestkey,
requestedfor,
requestedby,

sort - requestsubmittedon/duedate/requestid,

order - asc or desc,

requestid,
duedatestart(MM/dd/yyyy),
duedateend(MM/dd/yyyy),
submitdatestart(MM/dd/yyyy),
submitdateend(MM/dd/yyyy),
endpoint,
securitysystem,

firstname (requestedfor user),

lastname (requestedfor user),

assignee - list of usernames,

requesttype - list of requesttypes, (ADD,UPDATEACCOUNT,NEWACCOUNT,DEL,NEWROLEREQUEST,CREATEROLE,MODIFYROLE,CREATEUSER,UPDATEUSER,EXTENDACCESS etc),

approvedby - list of usernames,

rejectedby - list of usernames,

max, offset,

showentitlementdetails - true/false,

entresponsefields - if showentitlementdetails is true, sample - "entresponsefields":["description","soxcritical","customproperty1","syscritical","risk","privileged","status","confidentiality"]

exactmatch(true/false) - If true, returns records for which value of requestedfor, firstname, lastname fields matches exactly.

fetchdetailedstatus (true/false):
Default is false; if set to true, the requestandtaskstatus field returns detailed status for requests and associated tasks.
Note: This parameter is available from the Chicago GA Release (Updated on 26 February 2026).

requestandteaskstatus : EIC fetches the request and task status

  • Possible values when fetchdetailedstatus is false:

    • Empty

    • Request completed, Task pending

    • Request Completed, Task Completed.
      Note:
      Task Completed indicates that all tasks have reached an end state, either Completed, Failed, or Discontinued.
      Task Pending indicates that atleast one of the tasks is pending provisioning.

  • Possible values when fetchdetailedstatus is true:

    • Empty

    • Request Completed, Tasks Pending:
      The request approval is complete, but provisioning of all tasks is still pending.

    • Request Completed, Tasks In Progress:
      The request approval is complete, and provisioning of some tasks is complete, while others are still pending.

    • Request Completed, Tasks In Progress (Issues):
      The request approval is complete, and provisioning of tasks is still pending; however, at least one task has errored, failed, or been discontinued.

    • Request Completed, Tasks Completed:
      The request approval is complete, and all tasks have been successfully provisioned or reached an end state.

    • Request Completed, Tasks Partially Completed:
      The request approval is complete, and provisioning is completed for all tasks, out of which one or more tasks have failed or been discontinued.

    • Request Completed, Tasks Failed:
      The request approval is completed, and provisioning is completed for all the tasks where all the tasks either failed or were discontinued.

statusAsNewUI : true (default) /false. If true, EIC fetches the request Status as per the New User Experience, else EIC fetches the Status as per the Modern Experience.
Note: Available from the Amsterdam Early Adopter release.

request.description:
This API is used to approve/reject requests. Before running this call, first we need to run the API to retrieve request approval details in order to obtain the taskid and taskkey.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:
requestKey,
approver,
approvaldata (taskid, taskkey, action, requestAccessComments); action:1/2, 1 - approve, 2 - reject

requestAccessComments: Specify comments for access approval or rejection. Users must include access comments when the Require Approval Comments or Require Rejection Comments settings are enabled under Admin > Global Configurations > Requests. If users do not provide requestAccessComments the request approvals fail with the "requestAccessComments cannot be null or blank" reason.

Optional params:
comments

Note:

  • enableapprovervalidationinapprovalapi flag(with true/false values) can be added in configuration table to enable/disable validations when approver approvers the request.Default value of enableapprovervalidationinapprovalapi flag is null.

  • If an account request includes multiple entitlements and the user rejects the account but approves one of the entitlements, the entire request will be rejected.

    • Approve and Change End Date = "2"

    • Change End Date for Acc/Ent/Role = "5"

  • comments: (string) Any comments related to the approval

request.description:
This API facilitates certification consultations. It supports both individual and bulk actions and includes robust validation mechanisms to ensure data integrity and provide user-friendly error messages.

Request Body

  1. eid (Mandatory)

    1. Description: A unique identifier for the consultation request.

    2. Data Type: String

    3. Example: "EorL7pMBeAuxnuyjVx1c"

  2. comments (Mandatory)

    1. Description: Comments or notes related to the consultation process.

    2. Data Type: String

    3. Example: "Consult through api"

  3. certkey (Mandatory)

    1. Description: The key that identifies the specific certification task.

    2. Data Type: String or Integer

    3. Example: "3048"

  4. cert_userkey (Mandatory)

    1. Description: The key associated with the user involved in the certification task.

    2. Data Type: String or Integer

    3. Example: "29797"

  5. cert_entitlement_valuekey (Mandatory)

    1. Description: A key indicating the type of entitlement involved in the certification. Values can specify different types such as:

      • 0 for Account

      • -2 for Role

      • -4 for User

      • Any other value represents a specific entitlement key

    2. Data Type: String or Integer

    3. Example: "0"

  6. Assignee: (Mandatory)

    1. Description: User which we are going to assign or consult.

    2. Example: "3433"

  7. cert_accountkey: (Mandatory)

    1. Description: (string) Account key (if applicable).

    2. Example: "3214"

request.description:
This API can be used to approve or reject accounts or entitlements for a user manager attestation.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

attid - attestation id,

id - same as attid,

verifier - Indicates the approver/verifier username verifying the attestation request,

accounts -

1.accattkey - Indicates the account id which you want to approve/reject

2.userattkey - Indicates the user id which you want to approve

3.certified - Select the action you want to perform. For approval, mention ‘Yes’ and for rejecting mention ‘No’

entitlements -

1.accattkey - Indicates the account id for which you want to approve/reject for the respective entitlement

2.userattkey - Indicates the user id which you want to approve

3.certified - Select the action you want to perform. For approval, mention ‘Yes’ and for rejecting mention ‘No’

4.entattkey - Indicates the entitlement attribute key for which you want to approve/reject the respective entitlement

Either accounts or entitlements is mandatory.

Optional params:

users -

1.userattkey - Indicates the user id which you want to approve

2.certified - Specify the ‘Action’. Possible values are ‘Works for me’, ‘Does not work for me’, ‘Terminated’, and ‘No response’

comments

item.name: Approve Reject Campaign Account Entitlement Details

request.description:
This API is used to certify/revoke the user's access (account, entitlement) along with employment verification. When an approve or reject action is performed for a line item in a User Manager campaign, then only the latest comment sent through the API is retained in the comments field but all the comments (including actions) are stored in the audit trail/history.

From Release v23.8, this API now supports resetting of actions on roles within a certification.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

campaignid

certkey

verifier

accounts -

  1. accattkey
  2. userattkey
  3. certified (Can be Yes/No/Reset)
  4. comments

entitlements -

  1. entattkey
  2. accattkey
  3. userattkey
  4. certified (Can be Yes/No/Reset)
  5. comments

users -

  1. userattkey
  2. certified
  3. comments

Optional params:

bulkUpdate(Can be Y or N)

approveComment

rejectComment

doesNotBelongToMeComment

roleattkey

bulkValidations(If 'Y' the code works as is and all validations happen, if bulkValidations=' N' the code will skip validations for all the records passed)

request.description:
This API reassigns accounts, roles, or entitlements to a different user or certifier. The associated users for accounts, roles, or entitlements that are being reassigned, must be certified in Step 1.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

updateuser (can be Admin/Campaign Owner/Certifier/Delegate)

campaignid- Campaign ID or the primary key of the campaign table.

certkey- Certification key or the primary key of the certification table.

accounts- List of accounts. (You must provide either accounts/entitlements/roles)

entitlements- List of child entitlements. (You must provide either accounts/entitlements/roles)

roles - List of roles. (You must provide either accounts/entitlements/roles)

newassignee- New certifier or user to whom the certification will be assigned.

bulkupdate (can be Y/N)

bulkvalidation (can be Y/N)

bulkConsultAssociatedData (can be Y/N) This option enables you to specify whether to reassign all accounts, entitlements and roles related to the specified account/entitlement/role.

Optional params:

campaignname - Name of the campaign.

certificationname - Name of the certification.

reassignComments- Comments for reassigning the certification.

  • status: Specify the status of the risk. Specify activefor active risks or inactivefor inactive risks to create a risk.

  • priority: Specify the priority of the risk, such as low, medium, high, and critical to create a risk on the basis of the risk priority.

  • ruleset: Specify the appropriate ruleset associated with the risk that is required to be created on the request body.

  • description: Specify the description of the risk that is required to be created on the request body.

  • comments: Specify any comment related to the risk that is required to be created on the request body.

request.description:
This API updates an existing risk specified in the url as riskid.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Optional Parameters:

  • riskname: Specify the name of the risk that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • description: Specify the description of the risk that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • comments: Specify any comment related to the risk that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • priority: Specify the priority of the risk, such as low, medium, high, and critical to update an existing risk on the basis of the risk priority.

  • risktype: Specify the type of the risk. Specify SOD for adding one or more functions and view the SOD violations in the SOD Violation workbench or Crirtical Accessfor adding single function for restriction or critical access to update an existing risk.

  • status: Specify the status of the risk. Specify activefor active risks or inactivefor inactive risks to update an existing risk.

  • ruleset: Specify the appropriate ruleset associated with the risk that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • function1: Specify the appropriate function that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • function2: Specify the appropriate function that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • function3: Specify the appropriate function that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • function4: Specify the appropriate function that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • function5: Specify the appropriate function that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • businessprocess: Specify the appropriate business process name that is required to be updated on the request body.

  • analyticsname: Specify the analytics configuration name that is required to be updated on the request body.

response.name: Update an Existing Risk

request.description:
This API shows the entitlements under an existing function.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Mandatory Parameter:

  • $functionId: Specify the unique identification value of the ruleset.

Notes:

  • The condition position for the first entitlement must be 0 and should increment by 1 for each subsequent entitlement.

  • The next and previous operators can be used to construct complex SQL queries.

  • All the entitlements need to be added to the function to make any updates. Delta updates are not supported.

  • Next and previous operators can be used to build complex sql queries.

  • Operators can have values like ‘OR (‘.

  • Fetch Entitlements in Function response can be used as a payload for Save Entitlements in Function.

request.description:
The API shows the list of all SOD violations.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Optional Parameter:

  • rulesetKeys: Specify this specific rulesets that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • endpointKeys: Specify this specific endpoints that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • sodStatuses: Specify the status of SOD by choosing between OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RISK_ACCEPTED, CLOSED, REMEDIATED.

  • riskId: Specify the ID of the risk.

  • name: Specify the name of the risk.

  • function1Name to function5Name: Specify the function names associated with the risk.

  • riskpriority: Specify the priority of the risk by choosing between VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL.

  • customProperty1 to customProperty5: Specify the custom properties associated with the risk.

  • riskType: Specify the type of risk by choosing between NONE, SOD, CRITICAL_ACTION.

  • functionKeys: Specify this specific function that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • name: Specify the name of the function.

  • description: Specify the description of the function.

  • status: Specify the status of the function by choosing between ACTIVE, INACTIVE.

  • customProperty1 to customProperty5: Specify the custom properties of the function.

  • entitlementValueKeys: Specify this specific entitlement value that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • value: Specify the value of the entitlement.

  • status: Specify the status of the entitlement by choosing between ACTIVE, INACTIVE, DECOMMISSION_ACTIVE, DECOMMISSION_INACTIVE and DELETED.

  • customProperty1 to customProperty2: Specify the custom properties of the entitlement.

  • soxCritical: Specify the sox critical value of the entitlement by choosing between NONE, VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and VERY_HIGH.

  • sysCritical: Specify the sys critical value of the entitlement by choosing between NONE, VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and VERY_HIGH.

  • risk: Specify the risk value of the entitlement by choosing between VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL.

  • financial: Specify the financial value of the entitlement by choosing between VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL.

  • privileged: Specify the privileged value of the entitlement by choosing between VERY_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL.

  • accountKeys: Specify this specific account that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • name: Specify the name of the account.

  • type: Specify the type of the account.

  • status: Specify the status of the account.

  • securitysystemId: Specify the security system ID of the account.

  • customProperty1 to customProperty2: Specify the custom properties of the account.

  • userKeys: Specify this specific user that has been identified to be applied during a request.

  • userName: Specify the name of the user.

  • firstName: Specify the first name of the user.

  • lastName: Specify the last name of the user.

  • costcenter: Specify the cost center of the user.

  • employeeId: Specify the employee ID of the user.

  • jobCode: Specify the job code of the user.

  • jobDescription: Specify the job description of the user.

  • customProperty1 to customProperty3: Specify the custom properties of the user.

  • offset: Specify an offset value to retrieve a subset of SOD violation records starting with the offset value. Note: If you do not provide any offsetvalue, by default 0 is considered as offsetvalue.

  • max: Specify a max value to generate the maximum number of SOD violation records. Note: If you do not provide any max value, by default 15 is considered as max value.

  • field: Specify a field value to sort the SOD violation list based on the selection. You can choose between sodkey, riskId, riskName, and username. Note: If you do not provide any field value, by default sodkey is considered as field value.

  • order: Specify a order value to sort the SOD violation list based on the selection.

This API creates a password policy for your organization.

The Authorization must have a Bearer followed by a Token.

Mandatory Parameters:

  • policyname: Specify a unique name for the policy. You can include names such as ApplicationPolicy to better identify the type of policy.
  • expireafter: Specify length of time until a user password expires and must be changed. You can enter only numeric values.

Optional Parameters:

  • description: StartFragmentSpecify an optional description for the policy.

  • scope: Specify the application or user you wish to apply the policy to.

    • APPLICATION: Specify this option, if you want to assign the password policy to applications and cannot be used to validate passwords when users’ passwords are changed.
    • USER: Specify this option, if you want to assign the password policy at the user level. To change or reset user passwords in EIC, at least one password policy with USER scope must be available. This policy is invoked when a user password change or reset is initiated.

  • regex: You can specify regular expressions (regex) to define specific password patterns.

  • maxrepetedcharacters: Specify the maximum number of duplicate characters that a password can contain. For example, if you specify 2, then a password is not accepted if any character is repeated more than two times. You can set a value between 1 and 10 numeric characters.

  • minimumnumericcharacters: Specify the minimum number of numeric characters that a password must contain. For example: if you specify 3, then password should have at least 3 numbers. StartFragmentYou can set a value between 1 and 10 numeric characters.

  • minimumspecialcharacter: Specify the minimum number of special characters that a password must contain.

  • minimumalphanumericcharacters: Specify the minimum number of alphanumeric characters that a password must contain. For example, if minimum alphanumeric characters specified is 8 and if the password specified is 'john12' then the password is not accepted as it is short of two characters in this case with the configured value of 8 characters.

  • minimumuniquecharacters: Specify the minimum number of unique characters that a password must contain. Unique characters do not take into consideration duplicate characters.

  • minimumalphabetcharacters: Specify the minimum number of alphabetic characters that a password must contain.

  • minimumuppercasecharacters: Specify the minimum number of uppercase letters that a password must contain. For example, if minimum uppercase characters are specified as 2 and if password specified is John123 then the password is not accepted as only 1 Uppercase letter is specified in this case.

  • minimumlowercasecharacters: Specify minimum number of lowercase letters that a password must contain. For example, if minimum lowercase characters are specified as 2 and if password specified is JOHn123 then the password is not accepted as only 1 lowercase letter is specified in this case.

  • disallowlastpassword: Specify the frequency to prevent users from using any previous passwords whose change or reset process was initiated from EIC and not from the target applications. For example, if you specify 10, then users are allowed to reuse a password only after using 10 unique passwords. You can set a value between 1 and 25 numeric characters.

  • useblacklistdictionary: Specify YES to enable the the password blacklist dictionary. A password is rejected if its value matches a term in a dictionary that you configure.

  • blacklistedattributes: Specify the user attributes query to prevent users from using their user or account information.

  • minimumage: Specify the minimum period, in hours to limit how frequently users can change the password. For example, if you enter 2, then the user cannot change the password before 2 hours of creating the password.

  • regexdescription: Specify a custom regular expression error message if the end user password does not match the regex password policy configuration.

  • sendnotification: Specify true to send notifications to end users informing them of their upcoming password expiration. Notification emails can be sent to both user and account passwords.

  • notificationemailtemplate:

  • daystonotify: Specify the days, before user passwords expire (including service account owners) to send expiry notification email.

  • primaryidentificationattr: Specify the parameter to validate the identity of the calling user and make their details visible to the Helpdesk users.

  • secondaryidentificationattr: Specify the parameter to validate the identity of the calling user and make their details visible to the Helpdesk users.

  • resetpasswordnotification: You can send user password change or password reset notifications to end users. Specify the email template to customize the notification that the user receives.

, `minimumage`, `regexdescription`, `sendnotification`, `notificationemailtemplate`, `daystonotify`, `primaryidentificationattr`, `secondaryidentificationattr`, `resetpasswordnotification`

Mandatory Parameters:

  • endpoint: If the changePasswordAssociatedAccounts parameter is set to true then specify the list of endpoints (comma-separated).

  • validateagainstpolicy: Specify Y to ensure that your new password conforms to the USER scope password policy. If you do not want to apply the password policy, then specify N. The default value is Y.

  • updateUserPassword: If the changePasswordAssociatedAccounts parameter is set to true then specify true to update the user password and create the corresponding Change Password task. Specify false to create only the Change Password task. The default value is true.

  • setarstasksource - Specify true to set the source column in the arstasks table with the changeOwnPasswordFromAPI value. When the source column in arstasks table is set to the changeOwnPasswordFromAPI value then the pwdLastSet parameter is not set to 0 for Active Directory (AD). The default value is false.

request.description:
Use this API to run a job trigger in Saviynt Identity Cloud.

The following cases illustrate different scenarios on the usage of the analyticsAdvanceQuery parameter in the API:

Case 1: When you configure the "analyticsAdvanceQuery" within the payload, set the "defaultActionForAnalytics" as "true", and then execute the control from the API, it overrides the default action and the advanced query configuration within the job trigger.

Case 2: When you configure the "analyticsAdvanceQuery" within the payload, set the "defaultActionForAnalytics" as "false", and then execute the control from the API without performing the default actions configured in the control, it overrides the default action and the advanced query configuration within the job trigger.

Case 3: When you do not configure both the "analyticsAdvanceQuery" and the "defaultActionForAnalytics", the default action will depend on the configuration provided in the analytics job trigger.

The following cases illustrate different scenarios on the usage of the analyticsCategories parameter in the API:

Case 1: When you set the "defaultActionForAnalytics" as "true" to perform default actions for analytics controls by executing the control from job API, it will override the default action configuration within the job trigger.

Case 2: When you set the "defaultActionForAnalytics" as "false" to not perform default actions for analytics controls by executing the control from job API, it will override the default action configuration within the job trigger.

Case 3: When the defaultActionForAnalytics parameter is not set in the payload, the default action will depend on the configuration provided in the analytics job trigger.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

jobname

triggername

jobgroup

Optional params:

valueMap

createJobIfDoesNotExist - true/false

request.description:
This API creates a compressed file containing objects specified for T2P migration.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory params:

exportonline(can be true or false) - Determines if package needs to be exported online, exportpath(if exportonline is false) - Local path where export package will be generated, environmentname(if exportonline is true) - Name of the environment which can be created at the following path : Admin -> Global Configurations -> Misc -> Transport -> Add New Transport, objectstoexport - Supported objects : savRoles, emailTemplate, roles, analyticsV1, analyticsV2, globalConfig, workflows, connection, appOnboarding, userGroups, scanRules, organizations, securitySystems

Optional params:

updateuser - username of the user exporting the package, transportmembers(can be true or false) - option to transport members for selected objects such as SAV role, transportowner(can be true or false) - option to transport owners for selected objects, businessjustification

response.name: Export Package - Success

request.description:
Use this API to import a compressed file containing objects specified for T2P migration.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory Parameters

packagetoimport : Specify the complete path of the package that needs to be imported.
Note: The file must be stored in a location that Saviynt Identity Cloud can access.

Optional Parameters

  • updateuser: Specify the username of the user importing the package.

  • businessjustification: Add a business justification.

Supported Objects

The Transport feature supports the following objects:

  • savRoles

  • emailTemplate

  • roles

  • analyticsV1

  • analyticsV2

  • globalConfig

  • workflows

  • connection

  • ppOnboarding

  • userGroups

  • scanRules

  • organizations

  • securitySystems

response.name: Import Package - Success

request.description:
Use this API to check the status of the transport request (import, export, or transfer) and confirm whether it completed successfully or failed.

Note: This API returns the status of only those requests that have been processed using the enhanced transport feature.

The Authorization must start with Bearer followed by the Token.

Mandatory Parameters:

  • operation: Enter the type of transport request (export, import, or transfer).

  • filename: Enter the transport package zip file name in full (including the .zip extension).

  • requestid: If the operation parameter is set to import, then enter the request ID generated during the submission of the import request.

Starting with Release v23.11, you can use the REST API to fetch all the technical rules from the target system. Additionally, you can also perform the following actions:

  • Use the ruleId parameter to fetch a specific technical rule. The response displays details such as rule ID, rule name, description, and other attributes.

  • Filter the rules based on status and rulename.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory param:

ruleId

Optional param:

Offset - Specify the pagination.

Starting with Release v23.11, you can use the REST API to delete an inactive technical rules from the target system by specifying the ruleId parameter.

Note:

  • You can only delete an inactive technical rules.

    • the Rule is active.

    • the ID does not exist.

    • the user who perform the delete process is not a ROLE_ADMIN.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

ruleId

Starting with Release v24.5, you can use the REST API to delete inactive user update rules from the target system by specifying the ruleId parameter.

Note:

You cannot delete user update rules if:

  • The Rule is active.

  • The ID does not exist.

  • The user initiating the deletion process is not assigned the ROLE_ADMIN SAV role.

The Authorization must have Bearer followed by Token.

Mandatory param:

ruleId
